name: OS version and security patch level
plain: Reads OS version, API level and security patch date with no prompt.
meaning: Shows how up to date the phone is and its exposure to known bugs. A strong fingerprint bit and a fraud and compatibility signal.

android.note: Patch date is a yyyy-mm-dd string

limits.headline: Can see your phone's system version and security patch date, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app checks when it opens, often to show an update message
can: See your Android version, its build level and the security patch date
See your iPhone system version and build number
Show you a message to update, or turn off features that need a newer system
cannot: See which apps or settings you have changed
Tell who you are from the version alone
limits.differs: Android shows a security patch date apps can use. iPhone shows version and build only.

story.what_it_is: An app can read your system version and how recently it got security fixes.
story.for_you: You never see it. It shows whether your phone is up to date. An app can use that to warn you or to refuse to run on an old system.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to turn features on or off and to warn about risk. It is also a useful fraud clue and a fingerprint detail.

use_cases.example: A bank app warns you that your system is too old to be safe and asks you to update.
A game turns on a new graphics mode only on the latest system.
A fraud tool raises risk when a login comes from an old, unpatched system.
A company blocks work mail on phones missing the latest security patch.
An ad firm adds the exact system version to a fingerprint.
A developer checks which versions have the most users to decide when to drop old support.

story.android_note: Reads version, API level and security patch date with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Reads the system version with no prompt, but no patch date.
